story.title: When the Indus Broke Its Banks
story.subtitle: Hazard, exposure and impact of Pakistan's 2022 monsoon floods
story.byline: A data story built on UNOSAT satellite analysis, NDMA and PDNA figures
story.footer:
Sources: UNOSAT (flood extent & population exposure, WorldPop 2020), NDMA situation reports, 2022 PDNA, PMD, OCHA COD-AB boundaries, NASA GIBS/MODIS. Exposure figures are preliminary satellite estimates, not field-validated.
Built with the Mapbox Storytelling template.

chapters.title: A disaster in slow motion
chapters.description:
From mid-June to October 2022, an extreme monsoon, fed by record spring heat and glacier melt, flooded Pakistan from the Himalayas to the Arabian Sea. {{ e.people_affected|intword }} people were affected and {{ e.deaths|intcomma }} were killed.

chapters.title: The hazard: rain off the charts
chapters.description: Monsoon rainfall was 190% above the 30-year normal. In August, Sindh received {{ p.Sindh.rainfall_anomaly_pct }}% more and Balochistan {{ p.Balochistan.rainfall_anomaly_pct }}% more rain than normal (PMD). Flat, poorly drained plains became inland lakes.

chapters.title: Flash floods in the Swat valley
chapters.description: 26 August · Khyber PakhtunkhwaIn the mountains, rivers rose within hours. At Kalam, the Swat River tore through hotels built on the floodplain. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa lost {{ p.Khyber_Pakhtunkhwa.deaths }} lives.

chapters.title: The Kabul River overflows
chapters.description: 28 August · Nowshera & CharsaddaDownstream, the Kabul and Swat rivers converged on the Peshawar valley. Nowshera and Charsadda were evacuated as water rose to levels not seen since 2010.

chapters.title: Hill torrents sweep the plains
chapters.description: Torrents from the Suleman and Kirthar ranges hit Rajanpur and Dera Ghazi Khan and submerged Jaffarabad and Nasirabad. Balochistan recorded {{ p.Balochistan.deaths }} deaths and Punjab {{ p.Punjab.deaths }}. Blue shows flood water detected by the VIIRS satellite (UNOSAT).

chapters.title: The Indus becomes an inland sea
chapters.description: NASA MODIS false-colour image of Sindh on 4 Sep 2022. Water is dark blue, vegetation green. On the map, drag the slider to compare with September 2021.

chapters.title: Breaching Manchar Lake
chapters.description: 4 September · Dadu, SindhWith Pakistan's largest freshwater lake overflowing, engineers cut its embankment to save Sehwan and Bhan Saeedabad, deliberately flooding villages in Dadu and Jamshoro. UNOSAT detected {{ dadu.flood_km2|floatformat:0|intcomma }} km² of flood water in Dadu that week.

Districts are shaded by the share of their population exposed.

chapters.title: Water that would not leave
chapters.description: Weekly satellite passes show how slowly the water drained. By mid-October ({{ x.last_label }}), {{ x.last_flood_km2|floatformat:0|intcomma }} km² was still flooded and {{ x.last_exposed|intword }} people remained exposed, most of them in Sindh.
